annotation.title_clean: Opinion of the European Economic and Social Committee on (a) Proposal for a Regulation amending Regulations (EU) 2024/1689 and (EU) 2018/1139 (Digital Omnibus on AI) and (b) Proposal for a Regulation on the simplification of the digital legislative framework (Digital Omnibus)
annotation.title_en: Opinion of the European Economic and Social Committee on the Digital Omnibus on AI and the Digital Omnibus proposals
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union, C series (C/2026/3225)
annotation.summary_en: EESC opinion (adopted 18 March 2026) on the Commission's Digital Omnibus on AI and Digital Omnibus proposals. It supports simplification and risk-based, proportionate regulation while preserving GDPR and AI Act protections, workers' rights and social dialogue. It also calls for coherence with the Machinery and Medical Device Regulations and for aligning high-risk deadlines with harmonised standards.
key_provisions_or_claims: Supports risk-based regulation of AI and AI robotics, lighter for industrial/B2B uses, with 'human in command' safeguards
Calls for coherence between the AI Act and sectoral product rules (Machinery Regulation, MDR) to avoid dual conformity assessments
High-risk AI deadlines should align with availability of CEN/CENELEC harmonised standards and notified body capacity
Supports AI Office regulatory sandboxes and registration/notification when providers self-classify systems as not high-risk
Workers must be informed and consulted before AI is introduced at work; retain AI literacy obligation and a broad definition of personal data
